task_instance: Set up context engineering for a small sample Node.js project: author a CLAUDE.md rules file (tech stack, commands, conventions, boundaries, one style-pattern example) and a hierarchical PROJECT_MAP.md summary per the skill's Level 1/Hierarchical-Summary guidance, then use a 'Selective Include' task-context pack (per the skill's Context Packing Strategies) to implement the skill's own worked example task -- 'Add email validation to the registration endpoint' -- following the existing validatePhone pattern and the ValidationError convention, and verify with the project's real test suite.
evidence: Created sample-project/ (package.json, src/lib/validation.js, src/routes/auth.js, tests/auth.test.js) with a baseline validatePhone pattern and a registerHandler missing email validation. Ran `npm test` at baseline: 2/2 tests passed (node --test tests/*.test.js). Wrote sample-project/CLAUDE.md covering tech stack, commands, code conventions, boundaries, and a Patterns example, matching the skill's Level 1 template and satisfying its Verification checklist item 'Rules file exists and covers tech stack, commands, conventions, and boundaries'. Wrote sample-project/PROJECT_MAP.md as a Hierarchical Summary artifact. Wrote task-context-pack.md as a 'Selective Include' context pack for the task 'Add email validation to the registration endpoint' (mirrors the skill's own worked example), listing relevant files, the pattern to follow (validatePhone), and constraints (use ValidationError, follow validateX shape). Executed the pack's plan: added validateEmail() to src/lib/validation.js following the validatePhone shape, wired it into registerHandler in src/routes/auth.js with ValidationError on failure, and extended tests/auth.test.js with acceptance/rejection cases for email. Verified: `npm run lint` passed (node --check on both source files) and `npm test` passed 4/4 (node:test), including the new 'registerHandler rejects malformed email' and 'registerHandler accepts valid email' tests. All work done offline with only node/npm builtins already installed; no network access, package installs, or external services were used.
notes: No blockers encountered. The skill's core deliverable -- producing a rules file (CLAUDE.md) plus structured, selectively-scoped task context, and using it to drive a concrete, conventions-following code change that is verified by tests -- is fully achievable with local file/shell tools on an air-gapped workstation; it requires no network, credentials, or unavailable software.
